title: The video description is recorded at fetch and matched at selection (R1004)
body:
Implements `docs/plans/oracle/description-signal.md` — **OD-8 / R1004**, evidence **BL-11**.

BL-11 weighed reading descriptions as "an extra request per video". **In the built system that premise is false:** `fetch` already runs one full per-video extraction for every pending video, and the description arrives in it and was thrown away. `fetch_caption_track` becomes `fetch_video` returning both — the *same* call, and the one-client-per-run property is unchanged.

**The single most important line:** `load_cached` reads the new key with `.get`. Today a `KeyError` is caught and read as "no usable cache entry", so a strict read would silently invalidate every cache entry you already have and refetch the whole corpus — the opposite of R1004's "no forced refetch".

**Selection gains a third include rule**, after the title and before the threshold, recorded as `description_hit`. It yields **no mentions** and moves no distinct-canonical count: a description has no cue, so it has no timestamp, and R5 cuts every excerpt window from one. That is the load-bearing negative, and the blind tests assert it directly.

**The report gains two numbers, not one:** videos included on a description, and how many of those nothing else would have admitted. Only the second reads as R1004's "how many videos the signal added", because a video can satisfy two rules at once — and the blind author pinned a case where they differ.

**This does not reach the existing cache.** R1004 forbids a forced refetch, so the measured B850I case stays invisible on the entries already on disk until they are refetched. That is an operator action — and one refetch also serves R1013.

**Where the blind author was stricter than me:** it read the plan as setting *different* rules for a non-string description at the fetch boundary (becomes `""`) and in a cache record (coerced with `str`, so `850` on disk loads as `"850"`), and pinned both. And it kept only BL-11's hashtag line verbatim, inventing the title and cues and asserting on neither, with a table carrying no form reachable from the invented text — so the pre-slice exclusion is **demonstrated rather than assumed**, which is what OD-9's provenance rule asks.

Two cross-slice fixture collisions, mechanical: the author worked from base and could not see R1010 or R1012, so two `ThresholdReport` literals and the `selected.jsonl` key-set assertion needed the fields those slices added. The key set stays an **exact-set** assertion.

93 blind tests, 1091 passing.
